terms.latin: ērudītus, ērudītī m.; ērudīta, ērudītae f.
evidence: Cic. Fin. 1.26: quās quī tenent ērudītī appellantur (Lewis & Short s.v. ērudiō)
terms.comment: The participle of ērudiō, “instructed”, used as a noun or adjective: homō ērudītus, a learned man.

evidence: Cic. Brut. 114: doctus vir et Graecīs litterīs ērudītus (Lewis & Short s.v. doceō)

sources: Lewis & Short: erudio · Lewis & Short: doctus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 374.
